title: Severe Gastrointestinal Bleeding Risk
description: Combining Aspirin with Ibuprofen significantly increases the risk of upper GI ulceration and major internal bleeding. Ibuprofen also blocks the antiplatelet effect of low-dose Aspirin.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. Consult physician for gastro-protective analgesic alternative (e.g. Paracetamol).

title: Dual NSAID Toxicity & Renal Distress
description: Co-administration of Aspirin and Diclofenac (Voveran) markedly elevates stomach ulceration risk and causes acute reduction in renal perfusion.
recommendation: Do not take concurrently. Doctor verification required immediately.

title: Enhanced Ulcerogenic & Bleeding Hazard
description: Combining Aspirin with Aceclofenac (Zerodol) synergistically damages gastric mucosa, causing severe pain and potential gastrointestinal hemorrhage.
recommendation: Substitute NSAID painkiller with non-interacting analgesic under medical supervision.

title: Reduced Antiplatelet Efficacy
description: Pantoprazole may slightly inhibit CYP2C19 bioactivation of Clopidogrel, potentially dampening cardiovascular protection.
recommendation: Discuss timing separation or switching to an alternative acid reducer if clinically indicated.

title: Attenuated Antihypertensive Effect & Nephrotoxicity
description: NSAIDs like Ibuprofen reduce renal prostaglandin synthesis, blunting the blood pressure lowering effect of Telmisartan and raising acute kidney injury risk.
recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function closely if pain relief is required.

title: Risk of Lactic Acidosis
description: Metformin combined with IV iodinated contrast can trigger acute renal failure leading to dangerous systemic lactic acidosis.
recommendation: Withhold Metformin 48 hours prior to diagnostic contrast imaging.

title: Elevated Methotrexate Toxicity
description: Penicillins like Amoxicillin reduce renal clearance of Methotrexate, elevating blood levels and toxicity risks.
recommendation: Monitor serum methotrexate and blood cell counts closely.
